$schema: Tier pricing, weights and premium caps — single source of truth for what a USER is charged and what a request costs against their pool.
$canonical: tier-pricing.json at the monorepo ROOT. Edit only this file.
$sync: Mirrors are byte-identical GENERATED copies (each client bundles from its own root). After editing this file run: python3 scripts/sync_tier_pricing.py (use --check in CI). KlaatAI.Klaatu/tests/test_tier_pricing_contract.py asserts the gateway's _USER_COST_PER_MT / _UNIT_WEIGHTS_DEFAULT / cap tables match this file.
$note: Model/provider COST lives in model-pricing.json. This file is the sell side. Do not put provider cost here — clients must never display what we pay upstream.
$units: input/output are USD per 1 million tokens. weight is weighted request units consumed per user turn.

titan.label: Klaatu Titan
titan.note: Kimi K3 (2.5T). Auto-routing ENABLED 2026-07-29: reachable as the step above heavy via retry/context-pressure escalation, and directly by name or the klaatu-titan alias. Still never inferred from task shape. Entitlement (titan_allowed_for_plan) and the daily/monthly caps are what bound it — both DEMOTE to heavy rather than erroring.

$unitScalingNote: A5+A6 (2026-07-29). ONE RULE: units = min(measured cost of the turn / anchorUsd, the tier's weight). The weight is a CEILING, never a surprise — a titan turn costs AT MOST 15 units and usually less. Why cost and not the tier: titan's cascade spans 15x per turn (Claude-Opus-4.8 $0.0707, kimi-k3 $0.0359, deepseek-v4-pro direct $0.0046), so a flat 15 overcharges the cheap tail 4.8x, which is what forced the caps to look stingy. anchorUsd = one typical `code` turn. Fallbacks when cost is unknown: token-only estimate (weight x clamp(tokens/referenceTokens, minFactor, maxFactor)), then the flat weight — never 0. Clients MUST render this as an upper bound ("<=15x"), not a flat figure. Gateway: api/quota.py tier_unit_cost().

fx.$note: USD is the source of truth; every other currency is DERIVED — inr = round_to_nearest(usd * usdToInr, roundToNearest) + roundOffset, i.e. to the nearest x99. Yearly INR is monthly_inr x (usdYearly/usdMonthly), NOT a conversion of the yearly USD, so the annual discount is identical in every currency. RATE HISTORY: pinned at 85.4 on 2026-07-29 (reproduced the then-published 399/1299/2699/2599/8499 exactly, i.e. an implicit 10.9% India discount), then moved to the live market rate 95.86 the same day by founder decision — a DELIBERATE price rise of 7.7-25.1% (Starter 399->499). BEFORE CHANGING THIS NUMBER AGAIN: subscription_plans.razorpay_plan_id_*_inr point at Razorpay plans with the amount baked in at creation. Moving the rate without creating new Razorpay plans makes the card show one price while checkout charges another. Existing subscriptions stay bound to their old plan id, so current customers are grandfathered automatically.

$planPriceNote: Published monthly list price per seat. Lives here because the premium-cap budget is only meaningful against a price — the margin guard used to hardcode its own copy and drifted (it assumed Team $36 while we charge $30, so Team's ceilings were validated against revenue we don't collect). Must match Klaatu api/me_routes.py _PLAN_PRICE_USD and the subscription_plans table. Team is DELIBERATELY cheaper than Scale ($30 vs $32), so Team's caps must stay below Scale's.
$planDailyRequestsNote: Daily request allowance per plan, and whether it is a soft or a hard limit. `soft` = past it the request is served by a light tier and the header says so; `hard` = the plan's daily_limit, which does block. The unit pool is requests x unit_pool_multiplier, so one pure-Core day feels like 2x the old flat cap. Published because a plan recommender cannot work without it: these numbers were previously typed only into KlaatAi.Klaatu.UI/src/data/plans.ts, i.e. a marketing file, with nothing tying them to the gateway. Mirrors api/quota.py _PLAN_CONFIG soft_limit/daily_limit and _UNIT_POOL_MULTIPLIER; contract-tested.
$planTiersNote: Which EDITOR tiers a plan may route to at all — entitlement, distinct from plan_caps which bounds volume once entitled. Added 2026-07-29 because the /pricing/limits calculator recommended "Starter at $5/mo" for 600 titan requests a month: it compared raw request counts against the daily pool and knew nothing about entitlement, so it advertised a plan that cannot serve that tier even once outside a promo. `titan: "promo"` means the plan reaches titan ONLY inside a promo window (KLAATU_TITAN_PROMO_UNTIL, and for free also KLAATU_TITAN_FREE_PROMO > 0) — never a permanent feature, so no surface may sell it as one. Mirrors api/quota.py _PLAN_CONFIG allowed_tiers + titan_allowed_for_plan; contract-tested both ways so a tier can be neither silently added nor silently dropped here.
$demotionNote: Edges the gateway enforces (api/quota.py _DEMOTION_MAP). `reason` demotes to the web `core` tier even for editor clients — a pre-existing quirk kept here so clients render what actually happens, not what would be tidier. `code` is never demoted: it has no enforced per-tier cap, the weighted pool governs it.
